cause_assessment.idle_deletion: Plausible and supported by launch architecture plus provider documentation; provider event not available, so unconfirmed.
cause_assessment.resource_reclamation_or_usage_limit: Possible. Current balance is zero, but historical depletion not established. 12/24 hours are upper bounds, not promised lifetimes.
cause_assessment.oom_or_unhealthy_runtime: Possible; no terminal memory, exit-code or host-health evidence survived to confirm or exclude.
cause_assessment.ordinary_training_exception: No preserved terminal exception or failed status. An ordinary child exception would normally be caught and recorded by job(), rather than remove VM assignment.
cause_assessment.cli_or_token_only_failure: Earlier websocket trouble occurred while downloads continued. Final contents 404 plus subsequent zero server assignments establishes broader loss than only a detached local client; raw prune event alone would not.

recommended_pattern: Run actual supervisor/training work synchronously inside one notebook/kernel execution via blocking subprocess.run or job(), with an adequate client timeout and HTTP checkpoint backup separately. No artificial activity/keepalive or idle-policy evasion. Treat free runtime lifetime as interruptible.
improvement_candidates: Keep immutable source/protocol/checkpoint bindings and explicit continuation provenance.
Back up checkpoint, incremental training log, job exit status, and bounded memory telemetry while VM exists.
Record raw safe HTTP status and server assignment state separately from generic transport failure.
Treat last-success time as data availability; add real progress timestamps rather than trusting the launch-time training status.
If dependable multi-hour execution is required, use suitable paid/dedicated compute; no purchase was made.

sources.claim: Resources and idle/max lifetimes vary; free notebooks at most 12h; Pro+ continuous code up to 24h with sufficient units; these are not guarantees.
Colab team explains active/unacknowledged execution requirement and distinction between idle deletion and unhealthy-runtime deletion.
CLI uses active kernel work/interactions for liveness, no keepalive daemon; status BUSY/IDLE is CLI bookkeeping; runtime tokens refresh separately.

secrets_policy: No auth/session tokens, endpoint URLs, credentials, arbitrary command output, or raw sensitive history copied.
